content: The interaction between doxylamine and dopexamine involves opposing effects on sedation, with doxylamine increasing sedation and dopexamine decreasing it. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. Doxylamine, when combined with dosulepin, doxepin, droperidol, or other sedative agents, results in an additive increase in sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended in these cases. Erythromycin in its various forms (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) can reduce the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Intranasal esketamine and doxylamine can mutually increase each other's toxicity through enhanced sedation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Doxylamine, when co-administered with estazolam, eszopiclone, ethanol, etomidate, or other sedative agents, leads to an increase in sedation. Caution and monitoring are advised.
